title: feat(ui): Machines pane creates, edits and saves .mch machine files
body:
Follow-up to #287 (first slice: #382, the read-only Machines pane, merged).

## What changed
**Machines pane: create, edit and save `.mch` machine files.**
- **New:** **New blank** (mill, lathe or mill-turn, starting from the keys that kind requires), **New from template** (copies the selected machine), and **Edit machine**.
- **Property grid** with nine collapsible groups: General, Axes and travels, Rotaries and limits, Spindle range, Feeds, Tool changer and stations, Coolant codes, Live-tool codes, Units. Each field's tooltip names its key.
- **Validation.** `machine::validate` (from #382) runs live.
  - Each refusal is shown in red under its field. Refusals that belong to no field (for example a missing required axis) are listed above the grid.
  - **Save and Save As are disabled while any refusal stands**, so a refused file is never written.
- **Save / Save As.**
  - Save asks "Write <path>?" before writing.
  - Save As asks for a name in the user folder, and asks again before replacing an existing file.
  - Closing with unsaved edits asks before discarding them.
  - After a save the list is re-read and the new file is selected.
- **Shipped machines are read-only.** A built-in machine, or a file under `assets/machines`, opens read-only, and Save on it opens Save As.
- **Atomic write:** a temp file in the same folder, synced, then renamed.
- **Unknown keys are kept.** Edits are made on the file's raw JSON, so keys the editor doesn't know survive a save.
- **User folder:** `CAMCRAFT_MACHINES` (absolute paths only), otherwise `<platform data dir>/camcraft/machines`. Resolved in the app layer (`machine::store`), and the pane's list includes it.
- **Not an undoable project edit.** Saving a machine *file* queues no command and adds nothing to the undo history, per the issue. Assigning a machine to a setup is #384.
- **Code:** new app modules `machine/{store,fields,draft}.rs`; new UI `machine_file_editor.rs`. The existing Setup-pane `machine_editor.rs` is unchanged.
- `docs/decisions/383-machines-edit.md`

## How tested
- App `machine_edit` (10 tests):
  - round-trip keeping unknown keys;
  - a refused file is not written, with refusals per field and refusals with no field;
  - live-tool words all four or none;
  - each blank kind;
  - template and Save As, read-only shipped files, replace confirmation, bad names;
  - the atomic write leaves no temp file;
  - folder resolution with the override and for macOS, Windows and Linux (XDG);
  - the catalogue lists the user folder;
  - a bad field path is refused, not a panic.
- App `machine_library` 11/11 and `machine` 32/32. These tests never read the tester's real machines folder.
- UI `machines_` (7 tests, structural, no PNGs):
  - a template takes new travels and codes and saves to the user folder;
  - a backwards travel is refused on its field and nothing is written;
  - editing a shipped machine saves as a copy;
  - a hand-written user file keeps its unknown keys through an edit and save.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick`: app suites green. In ui, only the three headless-GPU tests fail (no adapter on this Mac), as on main.
- `clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Decisions to review
- **Key order is not kept.** The workspace `serde_json` has no `preserve_order`, so a saved file's keys come out sorted; the content, unknown keys included, round-trips exactly. Turning `preserve_order` on would change every JSON writer in the workspace, project files included, so it's left for a separate issue.
- **No coolant remove button yet.**

## Not exercised (draft until the contributor's GUI check)
A hands-on check in a release build. A test kit is prepared, sandboxed with `CAMCRAFT_MACHINES` so the real machines folder is untouched.

Changelog: The Machines pane creates, edits and saves .mch machine files: new blank or from a template, a property grid with per-field validation that blocks the save, atomic writes to the user machines folder, unknown keys kept (#383)

Fixes #383

title: feat(tools): draw a milling tool's holder as a revolved outline in the tool editor
body:
**Replaces #436**, which was opened from the old fork. GitHub detached that fork from this repo's network when NeoTech/Camcraft was briefly private, so it can no longer be updated. **Now stacked on #473** (the replacement for #399). It carries the merges with main through #461: `ToolBody` keeps #395's lathe frame and #431's insert zone alongside this PR's `spun` field. A file with `spun` together with `lathe` or `insert_zone` is refused by name.

**Stacked on #399** (tool editor body column), which is on #381 and #348. First slice of #93: the **holder** of a milling tool drawn as a revolved half-outline. The custom cutter/shank profile is a follow-up, hence `Refs #93`.

## What changed
- **`crates/tools/src/spun.rs`: `SpunProfile`**, a (z, r, arc) half-outline.
  - **Refusals by name, with 1-based point numbers:** 3..64 points; finite; r ≥ 0, z ≥ 0; closed to the axis at both ends; no interior point on the axis; segments ≥ 0.01 mm; an arc no tighter than its chord; the outline never running back down the axis; not flat; size caps.
  - **Arcs never under-read:** convex arcs are replaced by the polygon that encloses them, concave arcs by chords on the arc.
  - Its `bands()` feed #381's `HolderProfile` exactly.
- **Storage: a drawn holder is a `ToolBody`.** The outline's own bands are its envelope, so every #368 law reads it unchanged: fixture bands, `enclose`, the stamp, the fits/flutes/lathe refusals, undo and delete. Its facets are the revolve of the outline, so the sim draws it.
  - A new optional `ToolBody::spun` keeps the points for re-editing.
  - **No project version rung:** `ToolBodyDto` gets an optional `spun` key beside the facets, which are still written.
    - A reader that knows the key redraws the body from it.
    - A reader that doesn't judges the facets. Their ring points sit on the outline, so it can only over-report. A test pins this.
  - **Parametric means no body,** so a tool that never went Custom keeps identical stamps and toolpaths.
- **UI, milling kinds only.** The third column gets **Body / Profile** tabs; turning tools show the Body section unchanged, per the owner's comment on #93. The Profile tab has:
  - a Parametric / Custom toggle;
  - a points table with insert and remove (read-only in Parametric);
  - a to-scale side view: cutter and shank from the numbers, the holder amber when valid and red when not, flute/stickout/gauge ticks;
  - a live refusal by name;
  - **Apply profile**, which issues one undoable `SetToolBody::spun`.

  Parametric follows the draft numbers live; Custom keeps hand edits.
- `docs/decisions/93-spun-tool-editor.md`

## How tested
- tools lib: 21 pass (6 new).
- `tool_spun_profile` (6 tests):
  - bands exact;
  - a drawn flange is flagged by the fixture laws;
  - a parametric holder equals `HolderStack::cylinder`, and the stamp is unchanged after clearing;
  - undo and redo;
  - refusals, including into the flutes and on a lathe kind;
  - round-trip byte-identical, and a reader without the `spun` key over-reports.
- `tool_body` (8), `tool_body_view` (8) and `project_roundtrip` (69) pass.
- ui `tool_` tests: 22 pass. `tool_editor_snapshot` fails on purpose (release-lane, #359), because the tab row is new.
- `clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -D warnings` is clean.
- `scripts/gate.sh batch` fails only on tests already red on main:
  - #415;
  - the headless-GPU ui tests;
  - the release-lane snapshot;
  - `swarf_pose_continuity` (PR #351).

## Not exercised (draft until the contributor's GUI check; a test kit is prepared)
Follow-ups:
1. A custom cutter/neck/shank profile (`SpunProfile::cutter_of` is in place).
2. Fillet-at-vertex arcs.
3. Dragging points in the side view.
4. Spun profiles in the tool library file (#348).

Changelog: The tool editor draws a milling tool's holder as a revolved outline (points, arcs, live side view); the collision checks judge the drawn shape (#93)

Refs #93

title: feat(app): Pause, optional stop and go-home entries in the operation list
body:
**Replaces #427**, which was opened from the old fork. GitHub detached that fork from this repo's network when NeoTech/Camcraft was briefly private, so #427 can no longer be updated. This branch also carries the merge with main at #461.

## What changed
**A new program-entry kind: Pause (M0), Optional stop (M1) and Go home.**
- Entries sit in the operation list alongside operations, using the same `OperationMeta.order`.
- The new component `schema::ProgramEntry { action, setup, suppressed }` is not an `Operation`. So `setup::operation_order`, and every walk built on it, skips entries without per-walk carve-outs: the post tool gate and freshness, `rest::ahead_of`, the program sim, the setup sheet, the tool list, verify and `RegenerateAll`.
- An entry has no generated status, so it never holds the post as "not generated".

**Posting.** Each entry folds into the posted op before it, as that op's `PARAM AfterOperation` word (one hook in `posting::op_streams`, logic in `program_entry::posted_afters`).
- A Pause after Face1 posts byte-identically to setting Face1's after-action to Program stop. This is pinned for all three actions on Fanuc and Haas.
- Equal asks in one gap merge, and a program stop absorbs an optional stop.
- An entry after a suppressed op attaches to the last op that posts.
- Suppress and "Skip pauses and homes" mute entries just as they mute op actions.
- **Refused by name:**
  - an entry before every posted op;
  - a Pause and a Home in the same gap (the stream holds one after-word per gap);
  - entries on the Tormach post, which doesn't read `AfterOperation`, the same as the per-op action there today.

**Commands, all undoable.**
- New: `AddProgramEntry` (after a named row, or at the end of the active setup), `EditProgramEntry::with_action` and `::with_suppressed`.
- Reused: `ReorderOperation` (drag) and `DeleteEntity` (Del or the menu).
- `ReorderOperation`, `CreateOperation`'s append and `DeleteSetup`'s refusal now count over `program_entry::sequence`, which equals `operation_order` on documents without entries.

**UI.**
- Every operation-list menu gains "Add pause (M0) after", "Add go home after" and "Add optional stop (M1) after".
- An entry row uses the Post glyph, with its action and SUPPRESSED in the suffix. Its menu offers change action, suppress, delete and add after.
- Entries drag like op rows.

**Project file: no version rung.**
- An entry saves as `"kind": "entry"` plus an `entry` payload.
- A document without entries writes neither key, so its bytes are unchanged.
- An older reader refuses a file with entries (serde: unknown variant `entry`) rather than dropping the stops.

**Posted G-code:** only documents with entries change. No `.cps` was touched, and every existing golden is unchanged.

`docs/decisions/155-pause-home-entries.md`

## How tested
- App `program_entry` (7 tests):
  - add, reorder, delete, undo/redo, new-op placement;
  - an entry equals the per-op words byte for byte;
  - Fanuc and Haas goldens, and the Tormach refusal;
  - Suppress, Skip and action edits;
  - the gap rules;
  - project round-trip, save → load → save byte-stable;
  - walks unaffected: `program_ops`, tool list, setup sheet, sim verdict, rest digest, verification gate.
- UI (3 tests): the menu rows; an entry row with undo; a click-through from op menu to add pause, suppress, delete and undo.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick` (app and ui suites) passes except known failures:
  - `setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…`, red on main (#415);
  - the headless-GPU ui tests (no adapter on this Mac).
- `clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -D warnings` is clean. After the merge with main at #410, `program_entry` passes 7/7.

## Not exercised (draft until the contributor's GUI check)
- A hands-on check of the menus, drag and posted output in a release build. A test kit is prepared.
- Possible follow-ups:
  - Home-then-Pause in one gap (needs a compound after-word in every script that reads `afterModes`);
  - Tormach reading `AfterOperation`, which would change its output for existing per-op documents.

Changelog: Pause, optional stop and go-home entries can be placed between operations in the operation list; they post the same words as an operation's after-action (#155)

Fixes #155
